repo.description:
### Impact

In affected versions, attacker-controlled upload filenames used in chat message excerpts were rendered as unescaped HTML. An attacker who can upload a file with specially crafted markup in its filename could inject HTML into chat channel lists, chat summary emails, pinned message bars, reply/thread previews, and other excerpt renderers when other users view chat content.

This was addressed as a trusted-HTML rendering vulnerability, not as confirmed stored XSS. JavaScript execution was not demonstrated with Discourse's default security settings, and no confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact was identified. While the risk is limited, sites that have disabled or modified Discourse's default Content Security Policy (CSP) face increased exposure, and users should update to a patched version if available.

### Workarounds

No known workarounds for this issue.
repo.summary: Chat upload filenames rendered as raw HTML in excerpts
